sk-0qNY.title: Road numbers: 3 or 4 digits, rising to the east
sk-0qNY.summary: Besides highways, roads have 3-digit or 4-digit numbers. Roads numbered 500-560 run from west to east, and the 4-digit numbers also increase towards the east.

sk-1BOY.title: House numbers: white sign
sk-1BOY.summary: House numbers are usually on white signs with a thin red or black border.

sk-3quH.title: Bollard: orange double reflector, white back
sk-3quH.summary: Bollard with two orange reflectors on the front and a single white one on the back. Rarer blue and red versions exist. Only Czechia has the same design.

sk-4BtX.title: Sign: bilingual with Hungarian
sk-4BtX.summary: Several southern areas have a Hungarian majority, with street and information signs in two languages.

sk-5dso.title: Sign: bilingual town signs in Rusyn (Cyrillic)
sk-5dso.summary: In the northeast, town entry signs may also be in Rusyn, a Cyrillic-script language close to Ukrainian.

sk-5j6v.title: Google car: antenna with grey tape on top
sk-5j6v.summary: A car antenna with a grey piece of tape on top is visible in much of the Gen 3 coverage. Hungary, Romania and Bulgaria have this too.

sk-5mIL.title: Roofs: diamond-shaped tiles
sk-5mIL.summary: Roofs with diamond-shaped tiles are common here and in Czechia, and somewhat common in Hungary.

sk-8If0.title: Lamp posts: yellow with blue base
sk-8If0.summary: Yellow lamp posts with a blue base are mainly in the east, with one city in the centre as an exception. Only this exact colour pairing counts.

sk-9icq.title: Sign: hiking marker, colour strip between white
sk-9icq.summary: Hiking markers with one coloured strip between two white ones, sometimes shaped like an arrow. Far most common here and in Czechia, but also seen in Poland, Hungary and Germany.

differs.how: Similar markers exist but are much rarer
Similar markers exist but are much rarer
Similar markers exist but are much rarer

sk-EpW7.title: Sign: blue direction sign, small white arrows
sk-EpW7.summary: Blue direction signs with small white arrows. Czechia has large, filled-in white arrows instead.

differs.how: Czech arrows are large and filled in

sk-F7is.title: Guardrail: wide special type B
sk-F7is.summary: A special, wider type B guardrail that no other European country uses. Czechia uses it almost everywhere, while here other types appear occasionally.

sk-G4Pu.title: Chevron: white with red arrows
sk-G4Pu.summary: White chevrons with red arrows. Less often you find red on yellow. Czechia has the same.

sk-IJXC.title: Trams: only two cities
sk-IJXC.summary: Only two cities have trams: one in red, the other in yellow, blue and white. Buses use the same colours there, and red buses also appear in a third city.

sk-Isqn.title: Pole: wooden poles with white concrete supports
sk-Isqn.summary: Wooden poles with white concrete supports are somewhat more common than in Czechia. It is inconsistent, so use it only to settle a tough 50/50.

differs.how: Wooden poles with concrete supports are rarer there

sk-KXno.title: Roofs: grey metal, especially in the east
sk-KXno.summary: Grey metal roofs are very common, especially in the east. Czechia has far fewer outside the most mountainous areas.

differs.how: Far less common except in high mountains

sk-L3Hc.title: Sign: pedestrian, 5 stripes, person with belt
sk-L3Hc.summary: Two main pedestrian signs, both with five stripes: a simple person with a belt, or stripes packed close together. Germany has the same belted person, while Hungary's belt sits lower.

differs.how: Hungarian person has a distinctly lower belt

sk-L3Lc.title: City: biggest, with a large river through it
sk-L3Lc.summary: The largest city is also the only major city with a large river running through it.

sk-Lcdz.title: Landscape: very mountainous to completely flat
sk-Lcdz.summary: Ranges from very mountainous to completely flat. Czechia is generally hillier but less mountainous.

differs.how: Czechia is hillier but less mountainous

sk-MEKX.title: Poletop: short metal bars holding insulators
sk-MEKX.summary: Poletops usually have short metal bars that hold the insulators. Czechia has the same.

sk-MoJ0.title: Houses: well-kept panel blocks, bright colours
sk-MoJ0.summary: Prefab panel apartment blocks, often well maintained and painted in bright colours and patterns, sometimes also on smaller buildings. Poland and Hungary have a little of this too.

differs.how: Much less colourful and well kept
Much less colourful and well kept

sk-NtUD.title: Street sign: red, with a stylised font
sk-NtUD.summary: A town in the northwest has red street signs like Czechia's, but with a somewhat stylised font that sets them apart.

differs.how: Czech red signs use a plainer font

sk-PPvf.title: Phone numbers: 10 digits, starts with 0
sk-PPvf.summary: Phone numbers usually have 10 digits, the first 2-3 being the area code. Czech numbers generally don't start with a 0.

differs.how: Czech numbers generally don't start with 0

sk-Tqgf.title: Poletop: upside-down triangle with two braces
sk-Tqgf.summary: Two support bars under the metal bar make an upside-down triangle, seen sometimes here and in Czechia. Germany, Albania, Serbia and Romania have it too.

sk-VV2G.title: Sign: cycling sign with letter C, yellow post
sk-VV2G.summary: Cycling signs use the letter C as their symbol, found only here. They are styled like the hiking markers, including a yellow post on direction signs.

sk-bpnt.title: Landscape: wide valley between sharp mountains
sk-bpnt.summary: Two wide valleys in the north are surrounded by tall, often sharp mountains. Work out which direction the nearest mountain is to tell them apart. One has tall mountains to the northwest and lower hills to the southeast.

sk-cWSf.title: Road marker: black sign at bridge end
sk-cWSf.summary: In Gen 4 coverage, black signs often stand at the end of bridges, with the road number on the left.

sk-dRNN.title: Landscape: tall mountains centre and north
sk-dRNN.summary: The tallest mountains are in the centre and north. The flattest areas are in the southwest and southeast.

sk-dcqy.title: Street sign: white, blue text, thin red border
sk-dcqy.summary: By far the most common street sign is white with blue text and a thin red border. The same design exists in Czechia near the border, but Czech names never include the word "ulica".

differs.how: Czech street names never contain "ulica"

sk-dpYP.title: Sign: railway crossing with white rectangle
sk-dpYP.summary: The railway crossing sign sits on a white rectangular background. Czech ones have no background.

differs.how: Czech railway crossing signs have no background

sk-elyV.title: Google car: red Gen 4 car
sk-elyV.summary: A red Gen 4 car, also found in Czechia and some other European countries.

sk-fBwX.title: Houses: window shutters
sk-fBwX.summary: Window shutters are much more common here than in Czechia, and very common in Hungary.

differs.how: Shutters are much less common

sk-gKhC.title: Landscape: wide flat fields, far hills
sk-gKhC.summary: In the east: wide, flat fields with hills or mountains far in the distance.

sk-j8QN.title: Bollard: wedge shape, red front reflector
sk-j8QN.summary: A recently introduced standard bollard: a European wedge shape with a red front reflector, like Hungary's. Still very rare.

sk-lXWV.title: Google car: black Gen 4 car
sk-lXWV.summary: A black Gen 4 car, also found in Czechia and many other European countries.

sk-lm-2980.title: Sign: pedestrian, white edge, jacket at waist
sk-lm-2980.summary: Among 5-stripe pedestrian signs with a hat: here the sign has a white border and the person has a jacket draped at the waist. Czechia has an extra blue border and a tucked-in shirt.

differs.how: Czech sign has blue edge border and tucked-in shirt

sk-lyTP.title: Language: Ľ Ô Ä Ŕ Ĺ letters (vs Czech Ř Ě Ů)
sk-lyTP.summary: Slovak and Czech are close and both use acute accents. Slovak has Ľ, Ô, Ä, Ŕ and Ĺ, while Czech has Ř, Ě and Ů. South Slavic languages have no acute accents on vowels.

differs.how: Czech has Ř, Ě and Ů instead

sk-mWBL.title: Sign: small signs on double posts
sk-mWBL.summary: Small signs on two posts are fairly common. In Czechia only large signs sometimes have double posts.

differs.how: Small signs rarely have double posts

sk-mwCI.title: Plants: pine forests in the far west
sk-mwCI.summary: Pine forests are common in the westernmost part of the country.

sk-n27y.title: Houses: short side to the road, hip roof end
sk-n27y.summary: Many houses have the short side facing the road with the roof ending in a hip end. Very common in Hungary, less in Czechia.

differs.how: Less common there

sk-n4tG.title: Lamp posts: thick base with bolt pairs
sk-n4tG.summary: Lamp posts with a thick base fixed by opposing pairs of bolts are common here and in Czechia. The base shape varies.

sk-nCyZ.title: Sign: blue or green highway sign
sk-nCyZ.summary: Highway signs are blue or green with a white border right at the edge. Czech highway signs have a gap between border and edge.

differs.how: Border is separated from the edge

sk-nJkZ.title: Sign: very bold road sign font
sk-nJkZ.summary: Road signs normally use a very bold font. Czech signs use a much thinner one.

differs.how: Czech font is much thinner

sk-o2Ei.title: Google car: Gen 3 spring coverage
sk-o2Ei.summary: A lot of the Gen 3 coverage was shot in spring. Czechia has a lot of Gen 3 winter coverage instead.

differs.how: Czechia has lots of winter Gen 3 coverage

sk-otzr.title: Sign posts: temporary red-and-white striped squares
sk-otzr.summary: Temporary square sign posts coated in red and white stripes are common here and in Czechia.

sk-p0qp.title: Pole: wide round concrete, often in pairs
sk-p0qp.summary: Wide, round concrete poles, quite often attached in pairs. Czechia has the same.

sk-p6ai.title: Sign: painted border right at the edge
sk-p6ai.summary: The painted border on road signs usually runs right at the edge of the sign. On Czech signs a strip of the background colour separates the border from the edge.

differs.how: A background-colour strip separates border and edge

sk-qom3.title: Km marker: two sections split by black line
sk-qom3.summary: Kilometre markers have two sections divided by a black horizontal line, with the road number in the top section. Czech markers have no black line.

differs.how: Czech markers have no black horizontal line

sk-rf14.title: Pole: striped gas and water poles
sk-rf14.summary: Striped gas and water poles that look like snow poles often stand by the road. Utilities all over Europe use stripes, so check the location and other clues.

sk-rhBj.title: Houses: dark brown wood with white line art
sk-rhBj.summary: A village in the northwest has dark brown wooden houses whose walls are decorated with white line patterns.

sk-sfKN.title: Landscape: totally flat fields to the horizon
sk-sfKN.summary: In the west: completely flat farmland, rare elsewhere in the country. Czechia is rarely flat all the way to the horizon.

differs.how: Rarely flat all the way to the horizon

sk-u6tR.title: Sign post: open top, grey cap or thin black cap
sk-u6tR.summary: Sign post tops are open, or have a grey metal cap or a thin black cap. Most Czech posts have a thick black cap.

differs.how: Czech posts mostly have a thick black cap

sk-uRTI.title: Pole: yellow circle with number
sk-uRTI.summary: Concrete poles in two western regions often have yellow circles painted on them, usually with a number inside. Only circles count; other shapes appear elsewhere.

sk-uyAe.title: Trolleybus: green-yellow-white, matching poles
sk-uyAe.summary: Trolleybuses in one northern city are green, yellow and white, and the poles carrying the wires, often lamps too, are painted yellow and green to match.

sk-zSqS.title: Poletop: concrete pole with trident arms
sk-zSqS.summary: Concrete poles with a trident-like top, two arms angled upwards. The number of insulators varies. This is the rarest of the tops, but only found here and in Czechia.
